title: How a URL Loads in the Browser

scenes.line1: What happens when you load a URL?
scenes.line2: Can you walk through every step?
scenes.say: What really happens when you load a URL in your browser? Could you walk through every step if asked in an interview?

scenes.label: DNS
scenes.sub: Browser resolves the domain name to an IP.
scenes.say: First, the browser resolves the domain name to an I-P address using DNS, or Domain Name System.
Next, the browser opens a connection—using TCP or QUIC—then negotiates TLS for HTTPS. It sends an HTTP request and gets an HTTP response with the page’s HTML.

scenes.label: Rendering
scenes.sub: Browser parses HTML, loads resources, renders.
scenes.say: Finally, the browser parses the HTML, fetches extra resources like CSS and JavaScript, and renders the page you see.

scenes.question: Does rendering happen before DNS?
scenes.right: No, rendering happens after DNS, network, and HTTP steps.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Does rendering happen before DNS? No, rendering only starts after DNS, network, and HTTP steps are done.
